{{Quote|Since I have no wife or children, if I should die before my dear father, then everything I own shall belong to Zorba the Hutt, including&hellip;|Jabba the Hutt's Will|<ref name="rev" />}}
'''Jabba the Hutt's Will''', also known as '''JTHW''' and Jabba's "'''true will and testament'''," was a disputed document circulated by [[Zorba Desilijic Tiure]] in [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], entitling Zorba to the estate of his late son, [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. After his [[Death/Legends|death]] at [[Great Pit of Carkoon/Legends|Carkoon]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], no full will of Jabba's was discovered, and in lieu of a natural heir, the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord's]] [[Jabba's criminal empire/Legends|holdings]] throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] were seized by underlings and local authorities, as well as a few of his relatives to whom he had left some valuables. Zorba was [[Prison/Legends|imprisoned]] on [[Kip]] at the time and so was unaware of his son's death; upon Zorba's release, he collected the will's master copy from [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] and began to distribute it around the criminal underworld.

The document held up to scrutiny in Hutt courts; most of Jabba's estate was transferred to Zorba, and he wrested control of the [[Desilijic/Legends|Desilijic]] clan from the hands of Jabba's usurpers, [[Kumac]] and [[Jelasi]]. However, Zorba's leadership was unpopular, and his reign short-lived; before long several Hutt courts declared the will a forgery, and Jabba's criminal empire was once again absorbed by various factions. Zorba was deposed as Desilijic leader and went into hiding.

==Description==
[[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] left a simple prose will on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], which was read to a gathering of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt's]] relatives by a legal representative,<ref name="tjt">"[[The Jabba Tape]]"</ref> though this document was not widely known<ref name="rev" /> and discharged only some of Jabba's possessions.<ref name="negtc" /> Another will produced by [[Zorba Desilijic Tiure]] a year later was a simple [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] recording of Jabba dictating his will. As he had no offspring or life partner, Jabba simply stated that, should he [[Death/Legends|die]] before his father Zorba, his [[Jabba's criminal empire/Legends|entire estate]] should go to Zorba, and proceeded to list all of his properties, starting with those on Tatooine and [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]], [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]]. No executor was named, and there was no legal involvement in the testament. Jabba bequeathed nothing<ref name="rev" /> to his protégé [[Jelasi]],<ref name="gg11">''[[Galaxy Guide 11: Criminal Organizations]]''</ref> and claimed that he had no son;<ref name="rev" /> however, he had borne a child, [[Rotta/Legends|Rotta]], in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="cw">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> The recording, entitled JTHW, was stored in the [[Memory bank/Legends|memory banks]] of an archaic [[Droid/Legends|droid]] named [[CB-99]]. CB-99 was then hidden in a secret room in Jabba's [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|desert residence]] on Tatooine. Zorba claimed that Jabba made the will in secret, and CB-99's location was known only by father and son.<ref name="rev" />

==History==
{{Quote|Unfortunately, Jabba didn't leave a will, so naturally the Planetary Government of Tatooine took custody of his property&mdash;with the permission of the Empire, of course.|[[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Bertroff Hissa]]|<ref name="rev" />}}
Zorba Desilijic Tiure was the leader of the [[Desilijic/Legends|Desilijic]] clan and its [[Kajidic/Legends|criminal enterprises]] for centuries until he was [[Prison/Legends|imprisoned]] on remote [[Kip]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] for illegally mining [[Ulikuo gemstone]]s.<ref name="hnn">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|48|regional/13321_5.html|Zorba the Hutt Sentenced to 45 Years}}</ref> He was replaced first by his sibling [[Jiliac Desilijic Tiron|Jiliac]]<ref name="hutt gambit">''[[The Hutt Gambit]]''</ref> and then his offspring Jabba. Free from Zorba's poor leadership and financial mismanagement, the clan flourished, and Jabba ruled an expansive, lucrative criminal empire at the height of his power.<ref name="hhh">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20030911hutt|text=Hutt! Hutt! Hutt!}}</ref> However he was killed by [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] during the [[Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], and the Desilijic clan was thrown into a state of chaos, bereft of its influential and talented leader.<ref name="negtc" />

A slew of Jabba's close relatives, including his nephew [[Gorga Desilijic Aarrpo/Legends|Gorga Desilijic Aarrpo]], traveled to Tatooine to settle his estate. A legal representative of Jabba's read them the written will he had left, outlining what local properties he bequeathed each of them; however, the will discharged only a small amount of Jabba's legacy.<ref name="tjt" /> Jabba used the will to humiliate his obsequious nephew Gorga in front of the other Hutts, leaving him the entire holdings of the [[Bank of Jabba]], which in truth was a novelty ornament of little value.<ref name="tjt" /><ref name="FF140">{{FactFile|140|HUT 15-18|The Hutts}}</ref> However, few were aware of the will,<ref name="rev" /> and the majority of his properties remained unclaimed.<ref name="negtc" /> Despite an extensive search, no full testament left by Jabba could be found,<ref name="rev" /> and rival [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] fought amongst themselves for most of Jabba's estate,<ref name="negtc" /> while many properties were claimed by planetary authorities. Jabba had no clear heir,<ref name="rev" /> but after brutal internecine conflict [[Kumac]] and Jelasi became joint leaders of the Desilijic clan.<ref name="negtc" /> CB-99 remained on Tatooine, undiscovered in the palace, which was claimed by local authorities.<ref name="rev" />

Incarcerated on Kip, Zorba remained unaware of his son's death until he was released in [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]]. He learned of the events at Carkoon and retrieved Jabba's will from CB-99,<ref name="rev" /> seeing potential profit. After immediately circulating news of the "secret will" to his fellow Hutt kingpins,<ref name="hhh" /> Zorba traveled to Bespin to seize properties which he now claimed to own, with a coterie of [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] in tow. Cloud City [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], whose administration had appropriated Jabba's properties in the wake of his death, refused Zorba's claims. However, when Zorba played CB-99's recording to the baron, Calrissian was convinced of the will's legitimacy, and ultimately acquiesced to hand the real estate over to the Hutt.<ref name="rev" />

Calrissian may have taken the will at face value, but Zorba subsequently had to prove its validity through the Hutt courts.<ref name="negtc" /> Though many were surprised at its contents,<ref name="hhh" /> the document was deemed legitimate, and Zorba took control of Jabba's legacy. He usurped Kumac and Jelasi to become Desilijic clan leader. However, Zorba spent most of his time pursuing a vendetta against Jabba's killer, Leia Organa,<ref name="negtc" /> and was known for his lack of business acumen during his previous reign as clan leader:<ref name="hhh" /> the Desilijic clan dwindled further into obscurity, with [[Durga Besadii Tai|Durga's]] [[Besadii/Legends|Besadii]] clan becoming the most powerful criminal enterprise among the Hutts.<ref name="negtc" /> Desilijic tired of Zorba's leadership and sought to depose him. Hutt courts began to rescind their stamp of approval for Jabba the Hutt's Will, declaring it a forgery, and Zorba went into hiding.<ref name="hhh" />

==Controversy==
The legitimacy of Jabba the Hutt's Will was not universally accepted after Zorba produced it.<ref name="hhh" /> He claimed the will was a secret between himself and Jabba, and only the two of them were aware of its existence and location.<ref name="rev" /> Upon its dissemination in 5 ABY, the document startled many, who did not expect Jabba to be so generous to his father in death.<ref name="hhh" />

However, at least initially, the testament held firm in the face of scrutiny. Lando Calrissian accepted it as genuine, and so did Zorba's retinue of mercenaries.<ref name="rev" /> It was also recognized by the Hutt courts, who granted Zorba everything the document entitled him to. Additionally, a [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] scribe, writing long after<ref name="negtc" /> Zorba was suspected to have died,<ref name="hhh" /> accepted its legitimacy.<ref name="negtc" />

Ultimately, most of the Hutt courts opted to overturn their decision and declare the document a fabrication. However, the Hutts had ulterior motives to take this course of action: Zorba was a proven failure as clan leader, and under his leadership the clan's influence and revenue were dwindling, so a large number of his subordinates sought to topple him. Additionally, many Hutts stood to gain from such an annulment, with Zorba's inherited wealth divided up among a slew of Hutt interests.<ref name="hhh" />

The date of creation was not stated in the supposed recording of Jabba.<ref name="rev" /> However, as Zorba had been incarcerated over a quarter of a century before his son's death,<ref name="hnn" /> its existence predated Zorba's arrest in 22 BBY. Additionally, the droid that stored the JTHW file was antiquated and covered in dust when Zorba reactivated it in 5 ABY: it had been there so long that Zorba was unsure if its memory banks would still be functioning. The will also stated that Jabba had no children,<ref name="rev" /> but by 32 BBY he had produced one child.<ref name="cw" />

Jabba was suspected to have been coaching the ambitious Jelasi as his protégé and heir,<ref name="gg11" /> but the will left Jelasi nothing. That everything went to Zorba was startling to many of Jabba's former associates;<ref name="hhh" /> he and Zorba had not been close, and Jabba kept to himself, running his own business ventures without Zorba's interference. Jabba had no remorse about Zorba's imprisonment,<ref name="rd">''[[Rebel Dawn]]''</ref> and Zorba had hoped to gain from Jabba's astute leadership upon his release.<ref name="hhh" />

==Behind the scenes==
Jabba the Hutt's Will first appeared in the [[1992]] release ''[[Zorba the Hutt's Revenge]]'', which was made as part of the [[Adventures of a Jedi Prince|''Jedi Prince'']] series and written by [[Paul Davids|Paul]] and [[Hollace Davids]].<ref name="rev" />
